hypothesis: The only measured unroll candidate so far—two 8-character groups—was correct but slower than baseline (82.32 µs versus 55.00 µs mean). This contrasting four-group schedule computes each group’s table lookups before validating the group, then validates all four before writing output. It may expose more independent lookup work and amortize loop control, but code size and register pressure may make it slower still. No speedup is assumed.
notes: This proposal processes four 8-character groups (32 input characters, 24 output bytes) only when at least 37 input bytes remain, preserving the existing five-byte tail margin. Any invalid group falls back to the original scalar bytewise path from the start of the unrolled block. The recorded h01 attempt failed to build; the subsequent two-group candidate was valid but slower than baseline. No commands or new tests/timings were run here; the controller should check short and boundary lengths, padding, random valid data, and Lena before timing.
transformations: Added a scalar helper that performs all eight table lookups for one 8-character block before validating the lookup values.
Unrolled the decode loop to load and decode four independent blocks per iteration, followed by one combined validity decision and ordered output stores.
Set the bulk guard to 37 remaining characters so the loop reads only 32 input characters while preserving the original five-character tail margin.
Retained the original bytewise decoder for invalid input, padding, and remaining tails; added no explicit SIMD or parallel execution.
